thread:
maria: Morning team — taking the 0800->1600 handoff. I'm primary until 1600, @sam is secondary. Quick note: @alex is on PTO today so paging matrix has been updated (see runbook link). I think we have a small coverage gap 1300-1400 while I step into a customer call; leaving a warm-handoff plan below.

sam: ack. Ping me if anything spikes. I'll be on-call phone and Slack.

incident-bot: New alert created: HIGH latency spikes on /v1/generate (p95 > 2s) — alert id ALRT-87321 — triggered 1735056892 — severity: page.

maria: seeing the alert. Starting triage. First check: is this cross-region or single-region?

infra-bot: Metric summary: increased p95 in us-west-2 only. Error rate steady, connection counts normal. KV cache hit ratio dropped from 92% -> 45% over last 5m.

sam: looks like cache pressure. Could be the recent model rollout that bumped context length. Were there any recent rollouts? @jordan?

jordan: yep, there was a small canary of model v2.3 at 06:45 — config changed max_seq to 4096 for canary subset. Canary traffic is 5%. No errors reported initially but KV cache usage up.

maria: OK — mitigations: 1) rollback canary to v2.2 for all canary hosts, 2) increase KV cache eviction threshold, 3) route critical customers to dedicated nodes if available. I'll roll step 1 now.

maria: rolling canary back — command: ```redwoodctl rollout cancel --canary-id=canary-2026-03-14-06:45```

incident-bot: Page escalation: paging infra-lead and oncall-sre per paging rules (page if latency/throughput impact to >1% customers). Pages sent to: @ops-lead, @jordan.

ops-lead: got the page, en route. If rollback doesn't reduce p95 in 3m we should escalate to platform eng and consider fallback to quantized model.

sam: monitoring dashboard — p95 down from 2.4s -> 1.1s after rollback for canary hosts, overall p95 trending down but still 1.6s. KV hit still low.

maria: jotted runbook steps: "Cache pressure — short term: rollback model variant; mid term: bump cache size per host; long term: add adaptive KV eviction by workload." Link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cache-pressure. Also note customer-impact assessment: only interactive generation endpoints affected; embeddings unaffected. No 500s.

alex: FYI — I left a note on the runbook about the 4096 context change; we should gate that behind a perf regression test next time.

maria: agreed. For the 1300->1400 coverage gap: @sam will be primary for that hour. I'll DM handoff checklist now (prefix, recent alerts, mitigation steps).

sam: got the checklist. Also updated paging matrix: if multi-region impact, page oncall-sre + infra-lead + platform-rotation. If single-region but service affecting, page infra-lead + ops-lead. If degraded but <1% customers, send incident-bot annotate (no page).

jordan: seeing backend memory growth on some hosts; running `top` and heap dump capture now. If memory >80% for >2min, escalate to memory-sigs channel and consider host recycle.

maria: good. Anyone with customer questions — contact CS escalation alias; we've marked impacted orgs via the incident tracker (impact flag: degraded).

incident-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: ALRT-87321 returned to baseline at 1735057320 — p95 stable around 0.9s — root cause: model variant increased KV pressure.

maria: resolving on-call now — toggled postmortem draft in incidents repo: https://redwood.internal/incidents/ALRT-87321 — assigning draft to @alex for perf regression analysis. Please add any notes about runbook updates.

ops-lead: great work. Reminder on escalation etiquette: when paging a human, include: short symptom, region, immediate mitigations taken, and next steps. Example page body: "HIGH latency /v1/generate — us-west-2 — rolled back canary -> p95 down to 1.0s; taking heap dumps; may recycle hosts; bridging if recurs."

sam: small follow-up — I'll own the warm-handoff at 1255 so I can brief the afternoon oncall. Leaving a note here: 1255 check-in with @maria — confirm no outstanding mitigations, all caches stable, runbook updated.

maria: thanks — handing off now. Good luck, team :thumbsup:
